pc.marketAccessNote: Structured by wholesaler federations AND four B2B buying-group centrals, each aligning several networks: Viasso (Point S + Siligom, ~885 POS, Lyon), Eurofleet (Bridgestone's First Stop + Speedy + Côté Route, fleet accounts), FleetPartner (Continental's BestDrive + Eurotyre), and PRODY (Profil+ + Roady/Rapid Pare-Brise, ITM Mobilité). A relationship with one of these centrals opens several networks at once rather than one. Alliance Automotive Group (AAG) and Doyen/Autodis remain the largest pure wholesaler gateways. Two live disruption windows worth tracking: Feu Vert is being divested in 2026 (Alpha PE → Bassac, exclusive negotiation) and Midas International was acquired by Mavis (US) in June 2025 — both mean active supplier-relationship flux.

pc.marketAccessNote: Spain is highly distributor-led. Grupo Soledad and Grupo Andrés are the two strongest independent wholesale gateways, while NEX (the Euromaster/Rodi 50/50 joint venture) is a major strategic wholesaler but not an independent one. Soledad is especially strong in imported and multibrand supply, Grupo Andrés in large independent national distribution, and NEX in high-frequency delivery to professional workshops and the Euromaster/Rodi network. A new entrant should approach these three before trying fragmented workshop-by-workshop coverage.

pc.marketAccessNote: Italian wholesale is a few national groups plus a regional tier, not a two-name market. Fintyre Group (Fintyre, Franco Gomme and Gexpo Tyre; over 6M tyres a year across all categories) is the first anchor, followed by Univergomma, Gruppo Magri and Zuin, with Tagliabue Gomme Gross (TGG, €143.3M revenue in 2022) alongside them. Pneus In, Palmeri, Intergomma and regional importers such as Pneutec, Piùgomme and PR Sud make up the next tier, and manufacturers often use several of these at once for territorial coverage. TGG was acquired by Global Automotive Investments Holding BV in Dec 2023/Feb 2024, the same group that owns Van den Ban (already in your Netherlands list), a cross-border relationship worth exploring. Driver (Pirelli-owned, 400+ outlets) is the largest captive network and not an access route for a competing brand.

AKH says it is the largest player in the market and sells more than one million tyres a year; MARSO is a nationwide wholesaler with more than 1,000 resellers and about 30 own stores. Neither is clearly ahead on the evidence, and there is no third independent wholesaler of comparable scale. Major manufacturers also run Hungarian sales entities, so large-account business is split between distributors and the manufacturers' own direct sales. Apollo already has a Hungarian sales entity and a new Győr distribution centre to build on directly.

The 6.5M in the flow model is a customs-anchored estimate (range 5.9-7.0M) for passenger-car and SUV/4x4 tyres, not a published number, and it implies about 1.35 tyres per car, well above Austria and the Netherlands, so treat it with caution. pc.marketAccessNote: Switzerland has no tyre production, so everything is imported, and the model puts about four in ten tyres on a direct route from the manufacturers. The largest chains are captive: BestDrive (Continental), Euromaster (Michelin), First Stop (Bridgestone) and Premio (Goodyear). The independent trade is served by ESA, the purchasing cooperative of the Swiss motor trade with about 7,000 co-owners, by Swiss Tyre Group (17 shareholders, 25 sales points), by a few small regional wholesalers and by cross-border supply from German wholesalers and online platforms. For Apollo the openings are ESA, Swiss Tyre Group, regional wholesalers and online, including its own reifen.com. Growth here depends on getting listed and priced competitively, not on finding an importer.

pc.note: Caveat The research behind this card is an early draft. Its 16.9M passenger-car figure comes from a market report I could not open, so it is not confirmed, but it fits a real car parc of about 20M (0.84 tyres per car). PZPO data, which measure its members' sales to distributors and not the whole market, show passenger-car tyres up 7% in 2024 and SUV tyres up 23%. No channel split, wholesale split or distributor volumes are published, and entities are named players, not volume-ranked. Value figures differ by source ($1.77B on the earlier card, about $1.93B for all tyres in the research) and are not units.
pc.marketAccessNote: Inter Cars is the standout priority: Poland's dominant aftermarket distributor, with 250+ Polish branches, 600+ across 21 countries, its own Q Service Castrol independent workshop network and the Motointegrator.pl online shop. A relationship here has reach across the wider CEE region (Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Baltics, Balkans). Handlopex and JMK are established secondary wholesalers, far smaller. Online is the other gateway: Oponeo.pl is the leading tyre retailer online, although its claimed 30%+ share is not confirmed. The manufacturers' own Polish sales entities (Michelin, Continental, Goodyear, Pirelli) also supply the trade directly. The research gives no wholesaler volumes, so no distributor is ranked on tyre throughput.
